name: keeping the contract register
from: Commitments the firm makes — to itself, between units, to users — existing as prose or as nothing, with no record of which promises are mutual and which are one-directional.
to: A register in which a contract is recorded as a bilateral binding — both promise-sets stated, both duties and their correlative claims — so what a party may hold the firm to is read rather than renegotiated.
cost: Stating both sides of every commitment explicitly, including the ones a firm would rather leave implicit because one side is convenient and the other is not.
otherwise: Counsel remains deferred to humans indefinitely, and every commitment the firm has made stands on nothing any session can check.
